summary.name: GitOS
summary.one_liner: A free, open source native macOS git client that automatically uses the right GitHub account for each folder or repository.
use_cases: Pushing work and personal repos under the correct GitHub account
Generating commit messages from staged changes
Rebasing and resolving merge conflicts visually
Managing pull requests and issues inside a Mac git client
Keeping GitHub tokens in the macOS Keychain
summary.what_it_does: GitOS is a native SwiftUI git client for macOS. You assign folders or individual repos to GitHub accounts, and fetch, commit and push then use that account's sign-in and commit email without changing ~/.gitconfig. Tokens are stored in the macOS Keychain. It covers everyday git work such as reading history, rebasing without a text editor, resolving conflicts in three ways, handling stashes and worktrees, and managing pull requests and issues. It can write commit messages from staged changes using a signed-in Claude Code or Codex, or an Anthropic API key, sending the diff and recent commit subjects. Updates download in the background and install only when you click Restart to Update.
notable: Switches GitHub accounts automatically by folder or repo without editing ~/.gitconfig
Native SwiftUI app; open source under MIT license
AI commit messages can use signed-in Claude Code or Codex with no API key
Tokens stored in the macOS Keychain, separate from existing logins
caveats: Requires macOS 26 or later on Apple Silicon; Intel Macs and older macOS are not supported
Not notarized by Apple yet, so macOS requires the Open Anyway step once per version
Some organizations must approve the app, or private repos may appear as not found
